samples.summary: The blocking-report path of `cmdReview` (`blockingFindingsIn` → `renderBlockingFindings` → exit 1) is never executed by any test
samples.evidence: The only stand-in panel, `writeRecorderPanel` (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:856-870), always writes `panel.json` as `[{ id: "docs", conclusion: "success" }]`, so both CLI wiring tests take the green path. Nothing ever drives the command to a failing panel verdict, so `blockingFindingsIn` (spec-to-pr.mjs, unexported, new in this diff) has zero coverage: its `path.join(outDir, lens, "verdict.json")` layout assumption, the lens-id → directory-name mapping, and the exit-1 + `renderBlockingFindings` join are all untested. `renderBlockingFindings` is unit-tested only on hand-built `[{lens, findings}]` fixtures, which would pass even if `blockingFindingsIn` read the wrong path and returned `[]` for every lens — i.e. exactly the pre-change failure this feature exists to fix ("printed the ID of every failing lens and nothing else"). A recorder panel that writes a failure conclusion plus a lens verdict.json, asserting the finding text and key reach stderr and the exit code is 1, would close it.
searchedFor: read writeRecorderPanel and both CLI wiring tests

samples.summary: No test asserts that `--fresh` actually deletes round directories on a permitted real run
samples.evidence: Both `--fresh` CLI tests assert the opposite direction: "review --dry-run --fresh reports the reset round without deleting one" (line 434) and "review --fresh refused at the bound deletes nothing (real run)" (line 747). `roundDirsToClear` is unit-tested on names only (line 240). So if the `rmSync` loop in `cmdReview` were removed or mis-pathed, the whole suite would stay green while `--fresh` silently kept stale rounds and their carry-forward — the flag's entire purpose. A real run below the bound with a staged round-1 asserting the directory is gone is missing.
searchedFor: read the two --fresh CLI tests and roundDirsToClear test

samples.summary: The `--round N` explicit-override path is validated but never exercised
samples.evidence: `reviewArgsError` tests (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:330-342) only cover rejection of bad `--round` values. No test runs `review --round 2` (dry-run or real) to assert the round directory/report actually uses the supplied number, nor that `--round` interacts sanely with the bound (`--round 5` should be refused). A regression that ignored `args.round` and fell back to `nextRound` would not be caught.

samples.summary: `roundsOnDisk`'s documented ENOTDIR guard (a plain file named `round-1`) has no test
samples.evidence: The docblock for `roundsOnDisk` states the per-round `readdirSync` is wrapped specifically because "a plain file called `round-1` sitting in the base makes it throw ENOTDIR, which would break `priorFindingsFor`'s 'never throws' contract". The on-disk tests (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:255-292, 305-325) stage only directories and a `panel.json` *inside* a round dir; none creates a regular file named `round-N` in the base. The stated failure mode — junk in a shared temp directory turning into a failed review — is therefore unverified.
searchedFor: grep 'round-1' fixtures in the test file

samples.summary: `panelScript`'s default (env unset → sibling review-panel.mjs) is untested; only the test-only override branch is exercised
samples.evidence: `panelScript` is not imported in spec-to-pr.test.mjs (import list at lines 7-33) and is only reached through `WAFFLEBASE_REVIEW_PANEL` in the two wiring tests, i.e. every test takes the override branch. The branch every real invocation uses — resolving `path.join(HERE, "review-panel.mjs")` — is covered by nothing, so a wrong default path would ship green.
searchedFor: read the test file import block

samples.summary: Assertion that `roundDirsToClear` never yields `.` or `..` is true regardless of the implementation
samples.evidence: `assert.ok(!roundDirsToClear(["round-1", "..", "."]).some((n) => n === "." || n === ".."))` — the function maps through `roundsIn`, whose output is rebuilt as `round-${n}` from a `/^round-(\d+)$/` match, so `.`/`..` are unreachable by construction and the assertion holds for any plausible implementation. It adds no signal beyond the deepEqual on the line above.
searchedFor: read roundDirsToClear and roundsIn in spec-to-pr.mjs

samples.summary: The workflow drift guard asserts only that two literal strings appear somewhere in the YAML
samples.evidence: "the panel workflow's inline copy applies both selection filters" greps agent-review-panel.yml for `norm(f.severity) === 'critical' || norm(f.severity) === 'major'` and `f.lane !== 'backlog'`. The strings do exist (agent-review-panel.yml:1008-1009), but the test would keep passing if that inline block were moved into a dead/unused step, or if a third contradicting filter were added — it checks textual presence, not that the selection is applied to the findings written into `output.text`. Accepted as a best-effort guard given the copy cannot be imported, but its guarantee is weaker than the comment claims.

verdict.reason: The blocking-report path of cmdReview is genuinely uncovered. `blockingFindingsIn` (spec-to-pr.mjs:873) is unexported and reachable only through cmdReview's `blocking.length > 0` branch (spec-to-pr.mjs:1110-1119). The only two tests that actually spawn the review CLI with a panel (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:895, :952) both use `writeRecorderPanel` (spec-to-pr.test.mjs:855-870), which hardcodes `[{ id: "docs", conclusion: "success" }]`, so the branch is never entered; every other CLI invocation in the file (:366, :449, :518, :536, :975) is a dry run or an early argument/guard rejection. A repo-wide grep for WAFFLEBASE_REVIEW_PANEL finds no other driver, and no other test file spawns spec-to-pr review. `renderBlockingFindings` is exercised only on hand-built fixtures (:167-194, :398-409, :618-640), which would pass even if `blockingFindingsIn`'s `path.join(outDir, lens, "verdict.json")` layout or lens-id→directory mapping were wrong and returned [] for every lens — i.e. the exact pre-change failure (lens ids printed with no findings) would ship green. Major under the test-adequacy rubric: the central new behavior of the diff has no meaningful coverage of its file-reading half or of the exit-1 join.

searchedFor: checked exports imported by the test file
finding.summary: The blocking-verdict report path (`blockingFindingsIn` → `renderBlockingFindings` → exit 1) is untested: no test drives a panel.json with a blocking lens
finding.evidence: `blockingFindingsIn` (spec-to-pr.mjs:873) is a new, non-exported function that reads each failing lens's `verdict.json` from the round directory and feeds `carryForwardFindings` into `renderBlockingFindings` (:1112), then exits 1 (:1119). It is reachable only through the CLI, and the only CLI test that gets past the panel spawn uses a recorder stub that writes `[{ id: "docs", conclusion: "success" }]` (`writeRecorderPanel`, spec-to-pr.test.mjs:~838), so the blocking branch never runs. `renderBlockingFindings` is unit-tested on hand-built `[{lens, findings}]` fixtures (:180, :197) — which is exactly the both-ends-tested-but-not-the-join pattern the diff's own comments say this change exists to fix (see the comment at spec-to-pr.mjs:~860 about the wiring being where defects live). Nothing asserts that a blocking lens's verdict on disk actually produces a non-zero exit, the per-finding lines, or the "re-run for round N+1" guidance; a regression there turns a blocking local review into output a developer reads as clean.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. `blockingFindingsIn` (spec-to-pr.mjs:873-882) is non-exported and reachable only through `cmdReview`'s blocking branch (spec-to-pr.mjs:1110-1119: renderBlockingFindings → "re-run for round N+1" → process.exit(1)). I searched repo-wide for any test that could reach it: the only place that spawns the script is spec-to-pr.test.mjs, and the only panel-override hook `WAFFLEBASE_REVIEW_PANEL` (spec-to-pr.mjs:794) is used at spec-to-pr.test.mjs:897 and :954, both with `writeRecorderPanel` (:855-870) whose stub writes `[{ id: "docs", conclusion: "success" }]` (:865) — so `blocking.length` is always 0 and the branch never executes. All other CLI tests are `--dry-run` or bound/arg refusals that return before the panel spawn (:719, :767, :975, :518, :536). Grepping the distinctive strings "blocking lens verdict" and "re-run for round" across the whole tree finds them only in the source and the .trusted baseline — no assertion in any test. `renderBlockingFindings` is unit-tested on hand-built fixtures (:167, :185, :398, :618, :629) and `carryForwardFindings` separately, but the join (on-disk verdict.json → report → non-zero exit) has no coverage. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a major gap: a regression there silently turns a blocking local review into output a developer reads as clean.
